cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Mammary gland lobe (pink)

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: One of the major subdivisions of the mammary gland, composed of multiple lobules draining toward a lactiferous duct.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Contains the secretory glandular tissue responsible for milk production during lactation.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Embedded within fibrofatty tissue of the breast and arranged around the nipple.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Mammary gland lobule (pink)

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Small glandular unit within a mammary lobe, composed of clusters of secretory alveoli/acini.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Produces milk during lactation under hormonal stimulation.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Drains into small ducts that converge into larger lactiferous ducts.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lactiferous duct (black)

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Conveys milk from the glandular lobes toward the nipple.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs from the mammary gland lobes toward the nipple, receiving smaller ducts from lobules.

cards.question: Termination
cards.answer: Opens onto the surface of the nipple through a lactiferous opening.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lactiferous sinus (wider black part)

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Dilated portion of a lactiferous duct near the nipple.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Traditionally described as a small reservoir for milk near the nipple.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies immediately deep to the nipple and areolar region along the terminal part of a lactiferous duct.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Areola

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Pigmented circular area of skin surrounding the nipple.

cards.question: Contents
cards.answer: Contains sebaceous areolar glands, including glands of Montgomery.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Provides a lubricated, pigmented surface around the nipple and contributes to the nipple–areola complex during breastfeeding.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Nipple (mammary papilla)

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Projecting central part of the breast containing openings of the lactiferous ducts.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Provides the outlet for milk during breastfeeding.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Rich sensory innervation, predominantly from anterior and lateral cutaneous branches of thoracic intercostal nerves, especially around T4.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Located centrally within the areola.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Connective tissue and fat

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Fibrous connective tissue and adipose tissue surrounding and supporting the glandular tissue.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Provides structural support, shape and cushioning to the breast.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Fibrous septa extend between skin and deep fascia and contribute to the suspensory ligaments of the breast.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Fat

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Contributes substantially to breast volume, contour and cushioning.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Surrounds and separates glandular lobes and lies within the superficial fascia of the anterior chest wall.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: The proportion of fat relative to glandular tissue varies with age, hormonal state and body composition.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pectoral fascia and retromammary space

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Pectoral fascia covers pectoralis major; the retromammary space is a loose connective tissue plane between the breast and the deep fascia.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: The retromammary space allows the breast to move relatively freely over the pectoral fascia.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies deep to the breast and superficial to pectoralis major.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Loss of mobility over the chest wall can occur when malignancy invades the deep fascia or pectoral structures.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pectoralis major muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Adducts and medially rotates the arm; clavicular head flexes the arm; sternocostal head extends a flexed arm.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Lateral and medial pectoral nerves (C5–T1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Medial half of clavicle; sternum; upper six costal cartilages; aponeurosis of external oblique.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Areolar glands (glands of Montgomery)

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Enlarged sebaceous glands associated with the areola.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Secrete an oily substance that lubricates and protects the nipple–areola complex, particularly during breastfeeding.

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Located within the skin of the areola and may form small visible elevations.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Skin

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Epidermis and dermis covering the breast, continuous with surrounding thoracic skin.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Provides a protective external barrier and carries sensory innervation.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Superficial to the glandular and fatty tissue; connected to deeper breast tissue by fibrous septa.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Skin tethering, dimpling or peau d’orange can occur when breast malignancy affects suspensory ligaments or dermal lymphatics.
